mcp._refresh_token_reuse_interval_why: Seconds. Measured Nov 17 2026 about 11:10 AM CST from the Mac to the live token address with a made-up refresh token: 20 answered round trips, median 0.62 s, p99 1.70 s (60 sent 0.4 s apart; the other 40 were refused 429 by the token path's rate limit). The window must cover one renewal's round trip, so it is the p99 rounded up to whole seconds (the option takes whole seconds). Re-measure with a real renewal if the engine or the gateway moves.
mcp._refresh_token_no_end_seconds_why: An AI's access has no end of its own (the account owner, Nov 17 2026: how long access lasts is the person's choice, and by default it does not end). The refresh token's end is a date column, so 'no end' is this many seconds, 100 years, a date nobody reaches; the person's limit for an AI (consent.idleLimitDays, POST /connected/limit) shortens it.
mcp.ended_unused_words: Access ended: not used for {days} days.

delete_user._what: A signed-in person deletes their own account from /account (POST /api/auth/delete-user). enabled: on by default, because a members app must let a person delete their account in the app; a computer that must not offer it sets false (the address then answers 404). Before anything is deleted the business's own clean-up runs, through either of two ways that name no code of this tool. before_delete_module: a path from this folder, read as an import, exporting beforeDelete(user, request) (for a business whose code sits in this folder). before_delete_url: an http address on this computer (127.0.0.1 or localhost only, refused at start otherwise) that receives POST {user_id, email} signed as before-delete-url.mjs says, with before_delete_secret the name of the credential holding the key (the credentials folder) and before_delete_timeout_ms how long to wait. Either one failing (a throw, a refused connection, a timeout, any answer other than 2xx) keeps the account. null in all three: this tool keeps no rows of the business's own.

site._what: Who this sign-in is for: the one block the computer running it supplies (the tool's own files name no product, colour or logo). `name` fills every {{name}} in pages and words and is the passkey and authenticator issuer; `cli` fills {{cli}} (the command a person types to sign in again); `storage_prefix` starts every key the pages keep in the browser and the session cookie's name (__Host-<prefix>_session) unless session_cookie_name is set; `theme` {data_theme, scheme, theme_color} is the Screen Look theme the pages wear; `look_css` is that theme's resolved tokens; `share` {title, description} are the link-preview words (null: none); `links` are the head's manifest, icon and font links; `mark_svg` (text) and `wordmark_png` (base64) are the pictures, served from the assets path as mark.svg and wordmark.png (null: none drawn); `email` {palette, made_with_label} is the look every email is drawn in (email-message-html.mjs). The values below are a neutral stand-in.
site.name: Example

stop._what: A stop never drops a call (stop-without-dropping.mjs): /readyz answers 503 and the listeners keep taking calls for hold_ms (over two of the front door's 1 s health checks), then the calls held get up to grace_ms (longer than this tool's longest call, an email send bounded by its own email timeout) before the rest are ended.
